View filters as upward-closed families of sets and use the defining membership characterizations of `Filter.map` and `Filter.comap`.

- The first conjunct is exactly `map` membership: \(t\in \operatorname{map}(m,f)\) iff \(m^{-1}(t)\in f\).

- For the left side of the inner equivalence, expand `comap` membership into a witness \(u\in l\) satisfying
  \[
  f^{-1}(u)\subseteq s^{c}.
  \]
  This condition implies \(u\subseteq (f''s)^c\), so upward closure gives \((f''s)^c\in l\). Conversely, if \((f''s)^c\in l\), use that set as the `comap` witness and note
  \[
  f^{-1}\bigl((f''s)^c\bigr)\subseteq s^c.
  \]

- The right side of the inner equivalence is the basic introduction rule for `comap`: from \(t\in g\), take \(t\) itself as the witness to obtain \(m^{-1}(t)\in\operatorname{comap}(m,g)\).

Thus both universally quantified propositions inside the `Iff` hold independently, and the equivalence follows by applying each established proposition in the corresponding direction.
